events.title: Scala 3.0 released
events.summary: The Scala team released Scala 3.0 on May 4, 2021 — a major redesign with optional braces, union types, and a new compiler (Dotty).
events.about: Scala 3 simplified syntax (`if x then y`), added powerful type-level features, and improved Java interop. It aimed to keep Scala relevant for data engineering (Spark) and typed functional programming without the boilerplate critics blamed on Scala 2.

narrative.whyChosen: Scala 3 was a once-per-decade language revision for a major JVM language.
narrative.whyImportant: It reset Scala's design after years of complexity complaints from teams.
narrative.problemSolved: Scala 2's syntax and implicit-heavy style scared away teams who wanted JVM types without ceremony.

events.title: Erlang/OTP 24 released
events.summary: The Erlang/OTP team released OTP 24 on May 12, 2021 with JIT compilation, improved SSL/TLS, and enhanced observer tools.
events.about: OTP 24's JIT sped hot Erlang and Elixir code paths without changing semantics — a boost for Phoenix and RabbitMQ workloads. Updated crypto and socket APIs kept BEAM applications current for telecom, messaging, and fintech backends.

narrative.whyChosen: OTP 24's JIT was the biggest BEAM performance leap in years.
narrative.whyImportant: Faster Erlang benefited the entire Elixir ecosystem built on the same VM.
narrative.problemSolved: BEAM bytecode interpretation lagged behind JIT-equipped runtimes for CPU-heavy tasks.
